basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 27.' and it opens '(Vers. 27.) Dilatet Deus Japheth, et habitet in tabernaculis Sem. De Sem, Hebraei; de'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text:
(Vers. 27.) Dilatet Deus Japheth, et habitet in tabernaculis Sem. De Sem, Hebraei; de Japheth, populus gentium nascitur. Quia igitur lata est multitudo credentium, a latitudine, quae IAPHETH (יפת) dicitur, latitudo nomen accepit. Quod autem ait: Et habitet in tabernaculis Sem, de nobis prophetatur, qui in eruditione et scientia Scripturarum, ejecto Israele, versamur.

(Vers 29.) Et facti sunt omnes dies Noe nongenti quinquaginta anni. Ecce post diluvium trecentis quinquaginta annis vixit Noe. Ex quo perspicuum est, centum viginti annos generationi illi, ut supra diximus, ad poenitentiam datos, et non vitae mortalium constitutos.
